who: Elijah was a prophet of Israel in the 800s BC, under King Ahab and Queen Jezebel. He stood almost alone against the worship of Baal. He prayed down fire on Mount Carmel and rain after years of drought, and heard God in a still, small voice. The Bible tells no death: a whirlwind took him up to heaven.

tidbits.text: A pagan writer may remember the same drought. Under Ethbaal, king of Tyre and Jezebel's father, Menander says there was “a want of rain” for a year, until the king prayed and “there came great thunders”. Josephus quotes him.

The Hebrew behind “still” in the “still, small voice” is **demamah**: silence, stillness, calm. The Bible uses the word only three times. In Psalm 107 it is a storm gone quiet: “He calmed the storm to a whisper.”

cite.text: 1 Kings 19:12; Psalm 107:29; Strong's Hebrew 1827, at Bible Hub

tidbits.text: When a Samaritan village turned Jesus away, James and John asked Him, “Lord, do You want us to call down fire from heaven to consume them?” The King James Version adds “even as Elias did”. Jesus turned and rebuked them.
The Orthodox pass on a story from Epiphanius of Cyprus, a bishop of the 300s. When Elijah was born, his father Sobach saw angels wrap him in fire and feed him with flames.

cite.text: OCA, the Holy, Glorious Prophet Elijah

facts.label: Also called
facts.text: **Elias**, the Greek form, in the King James New Testament. **Elijah the Tishbite**. **Man of God**, as the widow and the king's captains called him. **Troubler of Israel**, as Ahab called him.

facts.label: From
facts.text: **Tishbe**, among the settlers of **Gilead**, east of the Jordan. Where Tishbe was is not certain, says the *Catholic Encyclopedia*.

facts.label: When
facts.text: The reigns of **Ahab** and his son **Ahaziah**, kings of Israel, in the **800s BC**.

facts.label: Family
facts.text: The Bible names **no parents, wife or children**. A later story names his father **Sobach**. Cassian and the Orthodox honour him as a man who stayed **unmarried** for God.

facts.label: How he looked
facts.text: A **hairy man** with a **leather belt** around his waist. From that alone, King Ahaziah knew who had turned his messengers back.

facts.label: His cloak
facts.text: He threw it around **Elisha** to call him, and rolled it up to strike the **Jordan**. When he was taken up, it fell, and Elisha took it.

facts.label: Wrote
facts.text: No book. The Bible keeps **one letter** from him, to King **Jehoram** of Judah, in 2 Chronicles 21.

facts.label: Taken up
facts.text: Beyond the **Jordan**, near **Jericho**, in a **whirlwind**. Fifty men searched for him for three days.

facts.label: Honoured by
facts.text: **Christians**, East and West. **Jews** set a chair for him at every circumcision. The **Quran** names him among God's messengers. The *Catholic Encyclopedia* found the **Druze** keeping a yearly feast for him on Carmel.

facts.label: Patron of
facts.text: **Rain** and good weather: the Orthodox pray to him in drought. The **Carmelites** long hailed him as their founder.

facts.label: In art
facts.text: Rising in a **fiery chariot**, letting his cloak fall to Elisha. Or in the wilderness, with a **raven** bringing him bread.

portrait.alt: A Russian icon on a gold ground: Elijah stands in a red chariot inside a great red circle, and lets his dark cloak fall to Elisha, who reaches up for it. Below, among stylised rocks, an angel stoops over Elijah asleep, with a cup and a bowl beside him, and Elijah sits in the wilderness under a raven.
portrait.credit: The Fiery Ascent of Elijah, an icon of the 1500s. State Historical Museum, Moscow. Public domain.
portrait.caption: A Russian icon of the 1500s, now in the State Historical Museum in Moscow. Elijah rises in the fiery chariot and his cloak falls to Elisha. Below, the angel wakes him with bread and water, and the raven feeds him. Public domain.

typeNote: The test names him for what came after his victory on Carmel. He ran into the wilderness, sat down under a broom tree and prayed, “I have had enough, LORD.” The desert fathers remembered him as a man who “loved silence”, and in Cassian's *Conferences* he is the first named for The Watcher, one of the test's seven roles.

west.text: His day in the **1916 Roman Martyrology**, and in the whole **Carmelite** order since 1551. Lutherans in the **Missouri Synod** commemorate him too.

east.text: The **Holy, Glorious Prophet Elijah**, for the **OCA** and the **Greek** churches. The **Russian Church** keeps the day on the old calendar, which is 2 August on today's.

feasts.note: East and West both keep him on 20 July, the *Catholic Encyclopedia* notes. Churches on the old calendar keep each date 13 days later.

said.lede: Jesus, His apostles, Ben Sira and the early Church, in their own words.

quotes.q: But I tell you truthfully that there were many widows in Israel in the time of Elijah, when the sky was shut for three and a half years and great famine swept over all the land. Yet Elijah was not sent to any of them, but to the widow of Zarephath in Sidon.
quotes.who: Jesus, in the synagogue at Nazareth. The crowd was so enraged that they tried to throw Him off a cliff.

quotes.q: Elijah was a man just like us. He prayed earnestly that it would not rain, and it did not rain on the land for three and a half years. Again he prayed, and the heavens gave rain, and the earth yielded its crops.
quotes.who: James, on the power of prayer

quotes.q: Then Elijah arose, the prophet like fire. His word burnt like a torch.
quotes.who: Ben Sira, in the book of Sirach. Catholic and Orthodox Bibles hold it; most Protestant Bibles leave it out, or print it among the Apocrypha.

moments.title: “Neither dew nor rain”
moments.text: Ahab married Jezebel, a king's daughter from Sidon, and served Baal. He built Baal a temple and an altar in Samaria. Then Elijah the Tishbite stood before him. “As surely as the LORD, the God of Israel, lives, before Whom I stand, there will be neither dew nor rain in these years except at my word!”

moments.title: Fed by ravens
moments.text: God sent him to hide by a brook east of the Jordan: “I have commanded the ravens to feed you there.” So he went. “The ravens would bring him bread and meat in the morning and evening, and he would drink from the brook.” Then the brook dried up, because there had been no rain.

moments.title: Obadiah
moments.text: In the third year of the drought, God sent Elijah back to Ahab. On the way he met Obadiah, who ran the king's palace. Obadiah feared the LORD. When Jezebel was killing the LORD's prophets, he had hidden a hundred of them in caves, and fed them. Now he was afraid. Ahab had searched every kingdom for Elijah. What if the Spirit carried Elijah off, and Ahab killed the man who brought the news? Elijah swore to him, “I will present myself to Ahab today.”

moments.title: Fire on the mountain
moments.text: Ahab met him with, “Is that you, O troubler of Israel?” Elijah had all Israel gathered on Mount Carmel, with the prophets of Baal. Each side would offer a bull and call on its god. “The God Who answers by fire, He is God.” Baal's prophets called from morning until evening. “But there was no sound, and no one answered.” Elijah rebuilt the LORD's altar with twelve stones, and had it soaked with water three times. Then he prayed, and “the fire of the LORD fell and consumed the sacrifice, the wood, the stones, and the dust, and it licked up the water in the trench.” The people fell facedown: “The LORD, He is God!” Then Elijah had the prophets of Baal seized. He took them down to the Kishon Valley and put them to death there.

moments.title: A cloud like a man's hand
moments.text: Elijah told Ahab, “Go up, eat and drink, for there is the sound of a heavy rain.” Then he climbed to the top of Carmel, bent down to the ground and put his face between his knees. Seven times he sent his servant to look toward the sea. The seventh time the servant said, “There is a cloud as small as a man's hand rising from the sea.” The sky grew dark, and a heavy rain began to fall. Elijah tucked his cloak into his belt and ran ahead of Ahab's chariot all the way to Jezreel.

moments.title: Under the broom tree
moments.text: Jezebel swore to kill him within a day. Elijah was afraid and ran for his life. He went a day's journey into the wilderness, sat down under a broom tree, and prayed that he might die. “I have had enough, LORD.” He fell asleep. An angel touched him: “Get up and eat.” By his head were a cake of bread baked over hot coals and a jar of water. He ate, and lay down again. The angel came a second time: “Get up and eat, or the journey will be too much for you.”

moments.title: The still, small voice
moments.text: He walked forty days and forty nights to Horeb, the mountain of God, and spent the night in a cave. “What are you doing here, Elijah?” He answered, “I am the only one left, and they are seeking my life as well.” He was told to stand on the mountain, for the LORD was about to pass by. A great wind tore at the mountains, “but the LORD was not in the wind.” Then came an earthquake, and a fire, but the LORD was not in them. “And after the fire came a still, small voice.” Elijah wrapped his face in his cloak and went out. God sent him back with work to do, and told him seven thousand in Israel had never bowed to Baal.

moments.title: The cloak on Elisha
moments.text: Elijah found Elisha son of Shaphat plowing with twelve teams of oxen. He passed by him and threw his cloak around him. Elisha ran after him: “Please let me kiss my father and mother goodbye, and then I will follow you.” “Go on back,” Elijah replied, “for what have I done to you?” Elisha slaughtered his oxen, burned their gear to cook the meat, and fed the people. Then he followed Elijah and served him.

moments.title: Naboth's vineyard
moments.text: Naboth would not sell Ahab the vineyard beside his palace: “The LORD forbid that I should give you the inheritance of my fathers.” Ahab sulked on his bed. So Jezebel wrote letters in his name. Two scoundrels swore that Naboth had cursed God and the king, and he was stoned to death. When Ahab went down to take the vineyard, Elijah was there. “So you have found me out, my enemy,” said the king. Elijah answered, “I have found you out because you have sold yourself to do evil in the sight of the LORD.” Ahab tore his clothes and put on sackcloth. God saw it, and put off the disaster until his son's days.

moments.title: The king who asked Baal-zebub
moments.text: Ahab's son Ahaziah fell through a lattice in his upper room. He sent messengers to ask Baal-zebub, the god of Ekron, if he would get well. Elijah met them on the road: “Is it because there is no God in Israel that you are on your way to inquire of Baal-zebub, the god of Ekron?” They went back and told the king. What sort of man was he? A hairy man, they said, “with a leather belt around his waist.” The king knew at once: “It was Elijah the Tishbite.” Ahaziah died, as Elijah had said.

moments.title: With Jesus, transfigured
moments.text: Jesus took Peter, James and John up a high mountain, and His face shone like the sun. “Suddenly Moses and Elijah appeared before them, talking with Jesus.” Luke says they spoke “about His departure, which He was about to accomplish at Jerusalem.” Peter offered to put up three shelters, “one for You, one for Moses, and one for Elijah.” Then a voice from a bright cloud said, “This is My beloved Son, in Whom I am well pleased. Listen to Him!”

miracles.lede: The ravens, the fire on Carmel and the rain are told in his life, above. These are the other wonders. At the altar on Carmel, he said where the power came from:

pledge.q: O LORD, God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, let it be known this day that You are God in Israel and that I am Your servant and have done all these things at Your command.

feature.title: wonders for a widow in Zarephath

items.title: The flour and the oil
items.text: When the brook dried up, God sent Elijah beyond Israel, to a widow. At the town gate she was gathering sticks. He asked her for water, then for bread. She had only a handful of flour and a little oil, and was about to make a last meal for herself and her son. “Do not be afraid,” he said. He told her to bake him a small cake first. God had promised that her flour and oil would last until the rain came.
items.quote: The jar of flour was not exhausted and the jug of oil did not run dry
items.witness: There was food every day for Elijah, the woman and her household.

items.title: Her son raised
items.text: Her son fell ill, until no breath was left in him. She cried out to Elijah, “What have you done to me?” He took the boy from her arms, carried him up to his room and laid him on his own bed. He stretched himself out over the child three times and cried out to the LORD.
items.quote: O LORD my God, please let this boy's life return to him!
items.witness: The boy lived. Elijah brought him down to his mother: “Look, your son is alive.” She said, “Now I know that you are a man of God.”

more.title: Fire on the king's soldiers
more.text: King Ahaziah sent a captain with fifty men to bring Elijah down from a hilltop. Elijah answered with the words below, and fire came down from heaven and consumed them. It happened again with a second captain and his fifty. The third captain fell on his knees and begged for their lives. Then the angel of the LORD told Elijah to go down with him, and not to be afraid.
more.quote: If I am a man of God, may fire come down from heaven and consume you and your fifty men.

more.title: The Jordan parted
more.text: On his last day, Elijah rolled up his cloak and struck the water of the Jordan. It parted to the right and to the left, and he and Elisha crossed on dry ground. When Elijah was gone, Elisha took up the fallen cloak and struck the water the same way, with the question below. It parted again.
more.quote: Where now is the LORD, the God of Elijah?

words.note: He wrote no book. His words are kept in 1 and 2 Kings, with one letter in 2 Chronicles. Outside the quiz's own section, every Bible line on this page is from the Berean Standard Bible. The exceptions are Sirach, from the World English Bible, and one King James line, named where it stands.

feature.q: How long will you waver between two opinions? If the LORD is God, follow Him. But if Baal is God, follow him.
feature.ctx: All Israel had gathered on the mountain, with the prophets of Baal. “But the people did not answer a word.”

quotes.q: I have not troubled Israel, but you and your father's house have, for you have forsaken the commandments of the LORD and have followed the Baals.
quotes.who: To King Ahab, who had just called him the troubler of Israel.

quotes.q: Shout louder, for he is a god! Perhaps he is deep in thought, or occupied, or on a journey. Perhaps he is sleeping and must be awakened!
quotes.who: At noon, to the prophets of Baal, who had called on their god since morning.

quotes.q: Answer me, O LORD! Answer me, so that this people will know that You, the LORD, are God, and that You have turned their hearts back again.
quotes.who: At the altar on Carmel, at the time of the evening sacrifice.

quotes.q: I have had enough, LORD. Take my life, for I am no better than my fathers.
quotes.who: Under a broom tree in the wilderness, running from Jezebel.

quotes.q: I have been very zealous for the LORD, the God of Hosts, but the Israelites have forsaken Your covenant, torn down Your altars, and killed Your prophets with the sword. I am the only one left, and they are seeking my life as well.
quotes.who: To God, in a cave on Horeb. He said it twice.

myths.claim: A chariot of fire carried Elijah up to heaven.
myths.truth: Not in 2 Kings. There a chariot of fire with horses of fire came between Elijah and Elisha, “and Elijah went up into heaven in a whirlwind.” The chariot ride is an old retelling. Ben Sira already has it: “You were taken up in a tempest of fire, in a chariot of fiery horses.” The icons paint it that way too.

myths.claim: Elijah was the last faithful believer left in Israel.
myths.truth: He said so, twice: “I am the only one left.” God answered that He had kept seven thousand “whose knees have not bowed to Baal”. Obadiah had already hidden a hundred of the LORD's prophets in caves. Paul reads it as hope: “In the same way, at the present time there is a remnant chosen by grace.”

circle.name: Moses
circle.text: Both met God on Horeb, the mountain of God. Both appeared with Jesus at the Transfiguration. Malachi names them side by side in the last lines of the prophets.

circle.name: John the Baptist
circle.text: He came “in the spirit and power of Elijah”, and dressed like him, with “a leather belt around his waist”. As Elijah stood up to Ahab and Jezebel, John stood up to Herod and Herodias.

circle.name: Ahab
circle.text: King of Israel. He married Jezebel and served Baal. He called Elijah the “troubler of Israel”, and his enemy. After Naboth's death he humbled himself, and God put off the disaster to his son's days.

circle.name: Jezebel
circle.text: Ahab's queen, a daughter of the king of the Sidonians. She killed the prophets of the LORD and swore to take Elijah's life. She arranged Naboth's death with letters in the king's name. Years later she died at Jezreel, as Elijah had said she would.

circle.name: Obadiah
circle.text: Ahab's palace steward, who feared the LORD. He hid a hundred prophets in caves, fifty to a cave, and brought them food and water.

circle.name: The widow of Zarephath
circle.text: A widow near Sidon, down to her last handful of flour. She fed him first, and he stayed in her upper room. Jesus named her at Nazareth.

circle.name: Elisha
circle.text: His successor, called from the plough. On Elijah's last day he would not leave him. He asked for a double portion of his spirit, and took up his cloak.

circle.name: Ahaziah
circle.text: Ahab's son and heir. After a fall, he sent to ask Baal-zebub, the god of Ekron, whether he would recover. Elijah turned his messengers back, and the king died as Elijah had said.

circle.name: Naboth
circle.text: A man of Jezreel who would not sell the king his family's vineyard. False witnesses had him stoned, and Elijah went to meet Ahab in the vineyard.

death.title: How he was taken up
death.big: The Bible tells no death. On his last walk with Elisha, a whirlwind took him up into heaven.
paras: Others knew the day had come. From Gilgal to Bethel, to Jericho and the Jordan, Elijah told Elisha three times to stay behind. Three times Elisha answered, “As surely as the LORD lives and as you yourself live, I will not leave you.” At Bethel and Jericho the sons of the prophets asked him if he knew his master would be taken that day. “Yes, I know,” he said. “Do not speak of it.”

They crossed the Jordan on dry ground, and Elisha asked for a double portion of Elijah's spirit. Then, “as they were walking along and talking together, suddenly a chariot of fire with horses of fire appeared and separated the two of them, and Elijah went up into heaven in a whirlwind.”
Elisha cried out, “My father, my father, the chariots and horsemen of Israel!” He saw him no more, and tore his clothes in two.
Fifty men searched for three days, in case the Spirit had set him down on a mountain or in a valley. They did not find him.
The Jewish historian Josephus, writing in the first century, puts it plainly: “Elijah disappeared from among men, and no one knows of his death to this very day.”

items.q: Tell me, what can I do for you before I am taken away from you?

items.k: When Elisha asked for a double portion of his spirit
items.q: You have requested a difficult thing. Nevertheless, if you see me as I am taken from you, it will be yours. But if not, then it will not be so.

later.title: What the early Church expected
later.text: Tertullian, writing about 210, held that Enoch and Elijah will come back and die at the end. They “are reserved for the suffering of death, that by their blood they may extinguish Antichrist.” The Orthodox still teach that Elijah will come before Christ's second coming, and be slain by the Antichrist.

cite.text: Tertullian, *A Treatise on the Soul*, chapter 50; OCA, the Prophet Elijah

extras.title: The promise of his return
extras.lede: The books of the prophets end with a promise: “Behold, I will send you Elijah the prophet before the coming of the great and awesome Day of the LORD” (Malachi 4:5). Here is how that promise was read.

items.title: John the Baptist
items.text: An angel told Zechariah that his son John would go before the Lord “in the spirit and power of Elijah”. Asked, “Are you Elijah?”, John said, “I am not.” Yet Jesus said of him, “if you are willing to accept it, he is the Elijah who was to come.” Some teachers of Tertullian's day read this as Elijah's soul born again in John. Tertullian answered that John had Elijah's spirit and power,
items.quote: not (observe) in his soul and his body.

cite.text: Luke 1:17; John 1:21; Matthew 11:14; Tertullian, *A Treatise on the Soul*, chapter 35

items.title: “Elijah must come first”
items.text: Coming down from the Transfiguration, the disciples asked, “Why then do the scribes say that Elijah must come first?” Jesus answered, “Elijah does indeed come, and he will restore all things. But I tell you that Elijah has already come.” John Chrysostom read it as two comings. John came before Christ's first coming, doing Elijah's work. Elijah himself, the man from Tishbe, will come before the second:
items.quote: In this sense Elias is come: but if thou wouldest seek the Tishbite, he is coming.

cite.text: Matthew 17:10-13; John Chrysostom, *Homilies on Matthew*, Homily 57

items.title: At the cross
items.text: When Jesus cried out, “Eli, Eli, lema sabachthani?”, some who stood there said, “He is calling Elijah.” Others said, “Leave Him alone. Let us see if Elijah comes to save Him.”

items.title: A chair at every circumcision
items.text: Jews wait for him too. At every circumcision, says the *Jewish Encyclopedia*, a carved chair is set for Elijah beside the one who holds the baby. It is called the chair of Elijah.

saint.big: Yes. He is honoured as a saint in the Orthodox and Catholic calendars, on 20 July. Lutherans in the Missouri Synod keep his day too.

churches.note: Church of England and Episcopal Church

paras: The Carmelites long held that their order went back to Elijah himself. A notice of theirs from the 1200s says that “from the days of Elias and Eliseus the holy fathers of the Old and the New Dispensation dwelt on Mount Carmel”. Historians doubted it, and a long quarrel followed. In 1698 Pope Innocent XII told both sides to be silent. The whole order has kept his feast since 1551.
The Litany of the Saints printed in Rome's calendar of 1969 calls on him by name, after Abraham and Moses.
The Orthodox sing of him on his day, and Rome's book of martyrs, in its 1916 edition, gives him one line:

quotes.q: An angel in the flesh, the foundation of the prophets, the second forerunner of the coming of Christ, glorious Elijah.

kin.text: Like Elijah under the broom tree, he knew weariness and the pull of quiet. His *Dialogues* open with him alone in “a solitary place, very fit for a sad and melancholy disposition”.
